{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Confections|Confectionery]]

'''Marshmallows''' are a light, spongy confection made primarily with sugar and gelatin, although some recipes contain egg whites.
 
==Ingredients==
*About 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (125 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] / 4.4 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) [[Cookbook:Powdered Sugar|confectioners' sugar]]
*3 ½ envelopes (2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] plus 2 ½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]]) unflavored powdered [[Cookbook:Gelatine|gelatin]]
*½ cup (125 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] / 4.2 oz) cold water
*2 cups (450 g / 16 oz) white [[Cookbook:Granulated Sugar|granulated sugar]]
*½ cup (160 g / 5.6 oz) light [[Cookbook:Corn Syrup|corn syrup]]
*½ cup (125 ml / 4.2 oz) hot water (about 115°F / 46.1°C)
*¼ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
*2 large [[Cookbook:Egg White|egg whites]]
*1 tsp [[Cookbook:Vanilla Extract|vanilla extract]]
*½ cup (125 ml / 4.2 [[Cookbook:Fluid Ounce|fl oz]]) [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|vegetable oil]]

==Procedure==
#Oil the bottom and sides of a {{convert/3|13|x|9|x|2|in|cm|adj=on}} rectangular metal [[Cookbook:Baking Pan|baking pan]], and [[Cookbook:Dusting|dust]] the bottom and sides with some confectioners' sugar.
#In bowl of standing electric mixer or in a large bowl, sprinkle gelatin over cold water and let stand to soften.
#In a 3 [[Cookbook:Quart|quart]] (2.8 L) heavy [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]], cook granulated sugar, corn syrup, hot water, and salt over low heat, stirring with a wooden spoon, until sugar is dissolved. 
#Increase heat to moderate and [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] mixture, without stirring, until a candy or digital [[Cookbook:Thermometer|thermometer]] registers {{convert|240|F|C}}, about 12 minutes. Remove pan from heat and pour sugar mixture over gelatin mixture, stirring until gelatin is dissolved.
#Using a standing or a hand-held electric [[Cookbook:Mixer|mixer]], [[Cookbook:Whipping|whip]] mixture on high speed until white, thick and nearly tripled in volume (about 6–10 minutes). 
#In a large bowl with cleaned beaters, whip whites (or reconstituted powdered whites) until they just hold stiff peaks. Beat whites and vanilla into sugar mixture until just combined. 
#Pour mixture into baking pan and [[Cookbook:Sifting|sift]] ¼ cup confectioners' sugar evenly over top. Cool marshmallow, uncovered, until firm (at least 3 hours and up to 1 day).
#Run a thin knife around edges of pan and invert pan onto large cutting board. Lifting up 1 corner of inverted pan, with fingers loosen marshmallow and let drop onto cutting board. 
#With a large knife trim edges of marshmallow and cut marshmallows into roughly 1-inch cubes. Sift remaining confectioners' sugar into a large bowl and add marshmallows in batches, tossing to evenly coat.

==Notes, tips, and variations==

* Try coating with toasted [[Cookbook:Coconut|coconut]] or [[Cookbook:Cocoa Powder|cocoa powder]] instead of powdered sugar.

steps.text: Oil the bottom and sides of a  rectangular metal baking pan, and dust the bottom and sides with some confectioners' sugar.
In bowl of standing electric mixer or in a large bowl, sprinkle gelatin over cold water and let stand to soften.
In a 3 quart (2.8 L) heavy saucepan, cook granulated sugar, corn syrup, hot water, and salt over low heat, stirring with a wooden spoon, until sugar is dissolved.

Increase heat to moderate and boil mixture, without stirring, until a candy or digital thermometer registers , about 12 minutes. Remove pan from heat and pour sugar mixture over gelatin mixture, stirring until gelatin is dissolved.
Using a standing or a hand-held electric mixer, whip mixture on high speed until white, thick and nearly tripled in volume (about 6–10 minutes).
In a large bowl with cleaned beaters, whip whites (or reconstituted powdered whites) until they just hold stiff peaks. Beat whites and vanilla into sugar mixture until just combined.
Pour mixture into baking pan and sift ¼ cup confectioners' sugar evenly over top. Cool marshmallow, uncovered, until firm (at least 3 hours and up to 1 day).
Run a thin knife around edges of pan and invert pan onto large cutting board. Lifting up 1 corner of inverted pan, with fingers loosen marshmallow and let drop onto cutting board.

With a large knife trim edges of marshmallow and cut marshmallows into roughly 1-inch cubes. Sift remaining confectioners' sugar into a large bowl and add marshmallows in batches, tossing to evenly coat.
